newsitem.title: USA: Jury deliberations resume in Food Lion/ABC case.
newsitem.headline: Jury deliberations resume in Food Lion/ABC case.

text.p: The jury deciding whether the ABC television network should pay punitive damages for its hidden-camera report on supermarket chain Food Lion Inc. was due to resume deliberating on Tuesday despite an impasse.
Federal judge Carlton Tilley told the jury on Friday to give deliberations another try even though the panel sent him its third note saying the 12-member panel was deadlocked.
"Your Honour, we can't come to an agreement and feel we can go no further," read the note signed by all jurors who weighed evidence in the grocer's fraud lawsuit for four days.
In 1992, ABC's "PrimeTime Live" broadcast a report that showed pictures of spoiled meat and unsanitary practices at two Food Lion stores. ABC is a unit of the Walt Disney Co.

Food Lion said its sales and stock price plunged after the broadcast, based on video obtained by two ABC undercover journalists who wore hidden cameras while briefly working for Food Lion as a deli clerk and meat wrapper.
Tilley said he hoped jurors would be refreshed after a long weekend break from the Greensboro, N.C. courthouse, following the observance of Martin Luther King's birthday on Monday.
